request: Check this flight: did a control fault occur, when, and where on the aircraft?

result.headline: No actuator control fault found; sensor-health error at 1.3 s and stuck airspeed and yaw-rate signals.
result.explanation: Attitude followed setpoints through a large transient at 1-9 s, so control tracking looks healthy. A sensor-health error at 1.3 s fits the airspeed (0 m/s) and yaw-rate (0 deg/s) channels being flat all flight.

evidence.quote: t=1.3 s mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
evidence.shows: A system sensor-health error logged at 1.3 s, with a low-voltage warning at the same instant.

evidence.quote: vehicle.airspeed 0 and vehicle.yaw_rate[yaw] 0 for t=0..26 while velocity[x] is about 10 m/s and yaw moves -85 to -52 deg
evidence.shows: Airspeed and yaw-rate readings are flat at zero and inconsistent with the motion, so those sensors or channels are stuck or unlogged.
Large ch[2] swing with a pitch-down and a 30 m altitude loss, while pitch follows the setpoint. This looks like a commanded recovery rather than an actuator failure.

evidence.quote: ch[7] 1.93e+03 and ch[0] 1.5e+03 constant all flight
evidence.shows: Two channels never move. Probably unused, or a fixed function such as arm or gimbal; not shown to be faulty.

checked.check: Attitude vs setpoint tracking (pitch, roll) over the flight
checked.result: Actual follows setpoint with about 1-2 s lag and settles by about t=10 s; no divergence or saturation.

checked.check: Actuator outputs for stuck, saturated or asymmetric channels
checked.result: ch[0], ch[6] and ch[7] constant; ch[2] has the largest excursion, 1210-1610 us, and never hits a limit.

checked.check: Airspeed and yaw-rate consistency with velocity and heading
checked.result: Both read exactly 0 all flight while ground speed is about 10 m/s and heading changes by about 30 deg.

effects.why: Altitude loss follows the pitch-down and low-throttle excursion; it is a consequence of the commanded manoeuvre.
Throttle dropped from 47% to 14% around t=1..3 and recovered. This is not shown to be a battery fault.

next_action.action: Inspect airspeed and gyro-yaw sensors and their logging configuration
next_action.why: Settles whether the zero airspeed and yaw rate are real sensor failures, which the 1.3 s health error may point to, or just unconfigured logging.
how: Check the pitot tube and airspeed sensor for blockage or disconnection
Check the sensor-health flags and the logged yaw-rate source
Review the battery voltage log around t=1 s
next_action.conditions: Powered on the ground, then a short hover or low-speed run with the same firmware and configuration.
next_action.baseline: A normal flight where airspeed tracks ground speed and yaw rate follows heading change.

outcomes.label: Airspeed and yaw-rate sensors dead
outcomes.means: Real sensor fault, consistent with the 1.3 s health error.
outcomes.then: Replace or repair the sensor and recheck.

outcomes.label: Sensors fine, channels unlogged
outcomes.means: Zero values are a logging artefact; no fault evidence remains.
outcomes.then: Fix logging and re-fly for a baseline.

unknowns: Which function ch[0], ch[6] and ch[7] drive
Battery voltage trace is not in the data
Whether the early 1-9 s manoeuvre was commanded or a recovery

already_answered.question: When was the first fault indication logged?
already_answered.answer: 1.3 s, a system sensor-health error together with a low-voltage warning.
already_answered.quote: t=1.3 s mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth

hypotheses.claim: A control-surface or actuator fault degraded attitude control.
hypotheses.because: Attitude tracked setpoints and no output saturated or stuck in a way that diverged from the commands.

hypotheses.claim: Airspeed and yaw-rate sensors are failed or stuck at zero, matching the sensor-health error.
hypotheses.because: Both read exactly zero all flight despite motion and heading change; the error at 1.3 s fits.

hypotheses.claim: The zero channels are an unconfigured or unlogged artefact, not a real fault.
hypotheses.because: Constant exact zeros can also mean the data was never populated.

hypotheses.claim: Low voltage at about 1.3 s caused the throttle dip.
hypotheses.because: Warning coincides with throttle falling from 47% to 14% at 1-3 s, but there is no voltage data.

events.why: Only explicit error; aligns with airspeed and yaw-rate channels reading zero.
Coincides with throttle drop; no voltage signal to confirm.

events.what: Pitch to -19 deg and 30 m altitude loss, 1-9 s
events.why: Tracked the setpoint; a transient recovery rather than a control failure.
